_loaderHint._comment: How recruits seed the dashboard with each fixture. Daemon URL TBD with conductor; the tempo-mock-jam ensemble is the canonical seed surface for stress data.
_loaderHint.step1_baseline: Start the daemon with `agent-tempo --dev daemon start` and bring up the mock ensemble: `agent-tempo --dev up --lineup tempo-mock-jam`. This gives a 5-player baseline ensemble with deterministic mock players (no real Claude calls).
_loaderHint.step2_seed_long_tail: For long-tail content: use the dashboard's CreateEnsemble wizard manually with names from `ensembleNames.longTail`, OR `cue` mock players to inject long descriptions via `set_ensemble_description`.
_loaderHint.step3_seed_stress: For stress content: same mechanism but with values from `*.stress` arrays. Note: agent-tempo enforces ENSEMBLE_NAME_REGEX + a max-length on names — synthetic stress strings may be rejected at the validation layer (good — flag as a finding if validation is missing). Use the dashboard's React DevTools or `__seedFixturesForTests` hook (TBD with eng team) to bypass server validation for layout-only testing.
_loaderHint.step4_seed_50_player: For 50-player ensembleSizeProfile.stress: mock-recruit 50 players against a single ensemble. Conductor can dispatch this via a one-shot script.
_loaderHint._alternative: If wire-seeding is too slow, recruits may use the dashboard's React DevTools to override props on a target component manually. The fixtures above are the source of truth for content values regardless of injection method.
